title: Impact of Upwind Pollution on Infant Mortality

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Two-Stage Least Squares (IV).  
We treat wind direction (z = 1 if the monitor is down-wind of the emission source) as an instrument for pollution exposure (x).  
Why IV: Wind direction affects ambient pollution concentrations but is plausibly exogenous to local socioeconomic conditions that directly affect infant mortality.  
Key assumptions  
1. Relevance: Wind direction must significantly predict pollution (Cov(z,x) ≠ 0).  
2. Exclusion / Exogeneity: Conditional on controls, wind direction affects infant mortality only through its impact on pollution, not through any other channel.  
3. Monotonicity (implicit in LATE): Upwind status never reduces pollution exposure for some locations while increasing it for others.  

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Impact of Upwind Pollution on Infant Mortality – IV study #
############################################################

# Load libraries
library(readr)        # fast reading
library(dplyr)        # data manipulation
library(AER)          # ivreg
library(lmtest)       # coeftest
library(sandwich)     # robust vcov

# 1. Read the data ------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s75_data.csv",
               col_types = cols(
                 y        = col_double(),
                 x        = col_double(),
                 z        = col_integer(),
                 controls = col_double()
               ))

# Quick inspection
print(head(df, 3))

# 2. Baseline IV regression ---------------------------------------------------
# First-stage: x ~ z + controls
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
summary(fs)

# Reduced-form: y ~ z + controls
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
summary(rf)

# Second stage 2SLS
iv_mod <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
# Robust (HC2) standard errors
iv_se  <- vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC2")
iv_res <- coeftest(iv_mod, vcov. = iv_se)

cat("\n===== Baseline 2SLS results =====\n")
print(iv_res)

# First-stage F-statistic (weak instrument test)
first_stage_f <- summary(iv_mod, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics["Weak instruments", "statistic"]
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic:", round(first_stage_f, 2), "\n")

# 3. Robustness checks --------------------------------------------------------
# (a) No controls
iv_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_noc_se <- vcovHC(iv_noc, type = "HC2")
cat("\n===== 2SLS WITHOUT CONTROLS =====\n")
print(coeftest(iv_noc, vcov.=iv_noc_se))

# (b) OLS as naïve comparison
ols_mod <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_se  <- vcovHC(ols_mod, type = "HC2")
cat("\n===== OLS (naïve) =====\n")
print(coeftest(ols_mod, vcov.=ols_se))

# 4. Key output ---------------------------------------------------------------
beta_iv <- iv_res["x","Estimate"]
se_iv   <- iv_res["x","Std. Error"]

cat("\n***********************************************************\n")
cat("Causal effect of pollution on infant mortality (2SLS):\n")
cat("  Coefficient =", round(beta_iv, 4),
    " | Robust SE =", round(se_iv, 4), "\n")
cat("***********************************************************\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. Higher pollution exposure (x) is expected to increase infant mortality (y).  
Magnitude: Because the variables are standardized (mean ≈ 0, sd ≈ 1), a 1-sd increase in pollution should raise the infant mortality index by roughly 0.4–0.7 standard deviations. Thus we expect the 2SLS coefficient on x ≈ +0.5 with a robust t-statistic clearly above 2, and a first-stage F-statistic well above the Stock-Yogo 10-rule (F ≈ 20–40) indicating a strong instrument.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Wind direction is used as an instrument for pollution exposure.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Upwind pollution exposure is found to significantly increase infant mortality.
